title: Isaiah Chapter 45 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 45 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 45 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 45.

questions.question: To whom does the LORD say, "I have holden thy right hand, to subdue nations before thee"?
questions.correctAnswer: Cyrus
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:1 states that the LORD speaks to Cyrus and holds his right hand to subdue nations before him.

questions.question: What will the LORD do before Cyrus according to Isaiah 45:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Make crooked places straight
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:2 says the LORD will go before Cyrus and make crooked places straight.

questions.question: What kind of treasures will the LORD give to Cyrus?
options: Treasures of darkness and hidden riches
questions.correctAnswer: Treasures of darkness and hidden riches
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:3 mentions that the LORD will give Cyrus treasures of darkness and hidden riches of secret places.

questions.question: For whose sake has the LORD called Cyrus by name?
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob and Israel
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:4 says that for Jacob His servant's sake and Israel His elect, the LORD has called Cyrus by name.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD says there is no God beside Him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:5 clearly states there is no God beside the LORD.

questions.question: From what directions does the LORD want people to know there is no God besides Him?
options: From the rising of the sun and from the west
questions.correctAnswer: From the rising of the sun and from the west
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:6 states that from the rising of the sun and from the west people shall know there is none beside the LORD.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 45:7, what does the LORD create?
options: Light and darkness, peace and evil
questions.correctAnswer: Light and darkness, peace and evil
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:7 says the LORD forms light, creates darkness, makes peace, and creates evil.

questions.question: What does the LORD command the heavens and earth to do in Isaiah 45:8?
options: Drop down righteousness and bring forth salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Drop down righteousness and bring forth salvation
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:8 commands the heavens to drop down righteousness and the earth to bring forth salvation.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 45:9 compares a man striving with his Maker to a clay pot striving with other pots.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:9 uses the analogy of a potsherd striving with other potsherds to describe one who contends with his Maker.

questions.question: Who is called "my anointed" in Isaiah 45:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Cyrus
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:1 clearly states that the LORD’s anointed is Cyrus.

questions.question: What will the gates do before Cyrus according to Isaiah 45:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Open and not be shut
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:1 says the gates shall be opened before Cyrus and shall not be shut.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD says He will not speak in secret or dark places according to Isaiah 45:19.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:19 states that the LORD has not spoken in secret or in dark places of the earth.

questions.question: What happens to the loins of kings before Cyrus according to Isaiah 45:1?
questions.correctAnswer: They are loosed
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:1 says the LORD will loose the loins of kings before Cyrus.

questions.question: In Isaiah 45, which event comes first?
options: The LORD holding Cyrus’s right hand
The earth opening to bring forth salvation
The gates of brass being broken
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD holding Cyrus’s right hand
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:1 mentions the LORD holding Cyrus’s right hand before other events like breaking gates and righteousness pouring down in later verses.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 45:7 states that the LORD only creates good things.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:7 says the LORD creates light and darkness, peace and evil, so He creates both good and evil.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 45 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 45 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 45:10, what warning does the LORD give concerning questioning one's parents?
options: Woe unto him that saith unto his father, What begettest thou?
Blessed is he that honors his father and mother
Honor thy father and mother that thy days be long
Children should always obey their parents
questions.correctAnswer: Woe unto him that saith unto his father, What begettest thou?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:10 explicitly warns woe upon those who question their father or mother with phrases like 'What begettest thou?' implying a rebuke against disrespect or doubt toward one's parents. This is reinforced by the context of divine authority in verses 11 and 12 where God asserts His sovereignty.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 45:11 teach believers to approach God regarding future events and His works?
options: Ask me of things to come concerning my sons, and concerning the work of my hands command ye me
Seek wisdom from earthly rulers instead of God
Ignore the works of God and trust in human strength
questions.correctAnswer: Ask me of things to come concerning my sons, and concerning the work of my hands command ye me
questions.explanation: Verse 11 encourages believers to actively seek God's guidance about the future and His works, showing the importance of trusting God's sovereignty. This complements verse 10's warning about questioning human authority and verse 12’s declaration of God as Creator and Commander.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 45:12 reveal about God's creative work and authority over the universe?
options: I have made the earth, and created man upon it: I, even my hands, have stretched out the heavens, and all their host have I commanded
God created only the heavens but not the earth
The earth was created by angels
Man created the earth through his own hands
questions.correctAnswer: I have made the earth, and created man upon it: I, even my hands, have stretched out the heavens, and all their host have I commanded
questions.explanation: This verse affirms God's direct involvement in creation and His supreme authority over the heavens and all their hosts, underlining the message in verses 10 and 11 about God's sovereign control and inviting trust in His power.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 45:13, what role does God assign to the one He has raised up?
options: He shall build my city, and he shall let go my captives, not for price nor reward
He shall conquer all nations by force
He shall live in luxury and ignore the needy
He shall rule only for personal gain
questions.correctAnswer: He shall build my city, and he shall let go my captives, not for price nor reward
questions.explanation: Verse 13 shows God's righteous plan for the one He raises up to build His city and free captives without seeking personal gain, emphasizing integrity and service. This continues the theme of God's sovereign direction introduced in verses 11 and 12.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 45:14 say about the nations of Egypt, Ethiopia, and the Sabeans in relation to God's people?
options: They shall come over in chains and make supplication, saying, Surely God is in thee
They will remain hostile and never submit
They will destroy Israel by force
They will ignore the God of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They shall come over in chains and make supplication, saying, Surely God is in thee
questions.explanation: Verse 14 describes the submission of these nations to God's people, acknowledging God's presence among them. This shows God's power over nations and supports earlier verses about His sovereignty and salvation plan.

questions.question: Isaiah 45:15 states, 'Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour.' What does this reveal about God's nature?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 15 acknowledges that God sometimes reveals Himself in hidden ways but remains the Savior of Israel, highlighting both His transcendence and His saving nature as emphasized in the surrounding context.

questions.question: What is the fate of idol makers according to Isaiah 45:16?
options: They shall be ashamed, confounded, and go to confusion together
They shall be exalted among men
They shall be blessed by God
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be ashamed, confounded, and go to confusion together
questions.explanation: Verse 16 clearly states the shame and confusion that will come upon idol makers, contrasting with the salvation promised to Israel in the following verse, and reinforcing the call to trust only in God.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 45:17 describe the salvation of Israel?
options: Israel shall be saved in the LORD with an everlasting salvation
Israel shall be destroyed by their enemies
Israel will be saved only temporarily
Israel's salvation depends on their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: Israel shall be saved in the LORD with an everlasting salvation
questions.explanation: Verse 17 promises everlasting salvation for Israel through the LORD, assuring believers of eternal security and highlighting God's faithfulness, which contrasts with the fate of idol makers in verse 16.

questions.question: What reason does Isaiah 45:18 give for the creation of the earth?
options: He created it to be inhabited, not in vain
He created it for it to remain empty
He created it as a punishment
He created it for angels only
questions.correctAnswer: He created it to be inhabited, not in vain
questions.explanation: Verse 18 emphasizes God's purposeful creation of the earth to be inhabited, underscoring His intentional design and refuting any idea of a meaningless creation, which ties back to His sovereign creative work in verses 11 and 12.

questions.question: Based on Isaiah 45:19, how does God communicate His message to the descendants of Jacob?
options: Not in secret or darkness, but in righteousness and truth
He does not communicate with them at all
questions.correctAnswer: Not in secret or darkness, but in righteousness and truth
questions.explanation: Verse 19 states that God speaks openly and rightly to Jacob’s descendants, reinforcing the trustworthiness of His word and encouraging believers to seek Him confidently, building on the themes of guidance in verses 11 and 12.

questions.question: What criticism does Isaiah 45:20 make about those who worship graven images?
options: They have no knowledge and pray to a god that cannot save
They have deep wisdom and true faith
questions.correctAnswer: They have no knowledge and pray to a god that cannot save
questions.explanation: Verse 20 rebukes idol worshipers for their ignorance and futile prayers to powerless gods, highlighting the folly of idolatry compared to the true God who saves, a theme consistent with verses 15 and 16.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 45:21, who is described as the only just God and Saviour?
options: The LORD, with no God else beside Him
The gods of Egypt and Ethiopia
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD, with no God else beside Him
questions.explanation: Verse 21 affirms the LORD as the sole just God and Savior, excluding all others, which emphasizes monotheism and the unique saving power of God as taught throughout the chapter, especially in verses 5 and 6.

questions.question: What invitation does Isaiah 45:22 extend to all the ends of the earth?
options: Look unto me, and be ye saved
Ignore the LORD and trust in yourself
Worship many gods to be safe
questions.correctAnswer: Look unto me, and be ye saved
questions.explanation: Verse 22 invites everyone to turn to God for salvation, reinforcing His exclusive power and saving nature, which ties closely to earlier themes of God's sovereignty and salvation in verses 17 and 21.

questions.question: Isaiah 45:23 declares that every knee shall bow and every tongue shall swear. What does this signify about God's authority?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 23 emphasizes the universal acknowledgment of God's sovereignty, indicating that ultimately all will submit to Him, consistent with the monotheistic and sovereign God theme seen throughout the chapter.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 45:24 say will happen to those who are incensed against the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be ashamed
questions.explanation: Verse 24 states that all who oppose the LORD will be put to shame, reinforcing the idea of God's ultimate justice and vindication, which complements the universal submission declared in verse 23.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 45 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 45.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 45, what does the LORD say about those who set up graven images and pray to gods that cannot save?
questions.correctAnswer: They have no knowledge
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:20 states that those who set up graven images and pray to gods that cannot save have no knowledge, emphasizing the folly of idolatry.

questions.question: What is the invitation given by the LORD to all the ends of the earth in Isaiah 45?
options: Look unto me, and be ye saved
questions.correctAnswer: Look unto me, and be ye saved
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:22 invites all people from all corners of the earth to look unto the LORD and be saved, highlighting the universal scope of salvation.

questions.question: What vow does the LORD swear by Himself in Isaiah 45?
options: That every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear
That the earth shall never be destroyed
That His people shall never suffer
That the sun shall stand still
questions.correctAnswer: That every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:23 declares that the LORD has sworn by Himself that every knee shall bow and every tongue shall swear to Him, emphasizing His sovereign authority. This is echoed in Philippians 2:10-11.

questions.question: In Isaiah 45, who does the LORD say shall come and make supplication, acknowledging that God is in thee?
options: The labour of Egypt, merchandise of Ethiopia and the Sabeans
questions.correctAnswer: The labour of Egypt, merchandise of Ethiopia and the Sabeans
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:14 describes that workers from Egypt, Ethiopia, and Sabeans will come in chains, make supplication, and confess that God is in thee.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He created the earth for, according to Isaiah 45?
options: To be a place of judgment only
questions.correctAnswer: To be inhabited
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:18 states that God created the earth not in vain but formed it to be inhabited, highlighting divine purpose in creation.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about the way He has spoken to the seed of Jacob in Isaiah 45?
options: He has not spoken in secret or in vain
He has spoken only in dreams
He has spoken only through angels
He has spoken only in parables
questions.correctAnswer: He has not spoken in secret or in vain
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:19 emphasizes that the LORD has not spoken in secret or darkness, nor told Jacob to seek Him in vain; His words are righteous and right.

questions.question: Which title does the LORD use to describe Himself in Isaiah 45:21?
options: A just God and a Saviour
questions.correctAnswer: A just God and a Saviour
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:21 identifies the LORD as a just God and a Saviour, affirming His righteousness and redemptive role, which is foundational to biblical theology.

questions.question: In Isaiah 45, what does the LORD say about those who strive with their Maker?
questions.correctAnswer: Woe unto them
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:9 pronounces woe on those who contend with their Maker, illustrating the folly of questioning God's sovereign workmanship.

questions.question: Who is described as the LORD's anointed in Isaiah 45?
questions.correctAnswer: Cyrus
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:1 calls Cyrus the LORD's anointed, whom God uses to subdue nations and open gates, foreshadowing God's use of a foreign ruler for His purposes.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Isaiah 45:23, where every knee shall bow and every tongue shall swear?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:23 uses inclusio by framing the universal submission to God with both physical and verbal acts—kneeling and swearing—enclosing the theme of divine sovereignty. This literary feature emphasizes completeness.

questions.question: What Hebrew word concept in Isaiah 45:22 emphasizes the universal nature of God's salvation?
questions.correctAnswer: Ends of the earth
questions.explanation: The phrase 'all the ends of the earth' in Isaiah 45:22 highlights the Hebrew concept of God's salvation extending universally, beyond Israel to all nations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 45, what will happen to those who are incensed against the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be ashamed
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:24 says that those who are angry against the LORD shall be ashamed, indicating the futility of opposing God.

questions.question: What is the significance of the name 'Cyrus' in the context of Isaiah 45 and biblical history?
options: He is the Persian king chosen by God to free Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He is the Persian king chosen by God to free Israel
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:1 describes Cyrus as the LORD's anointed, a Persian king chosen to liberate Israel from Babylonian captivity, fulfilling prophecy and illustrating divine sovereignty over nations.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 45 states that God created both light and darkness, peace and evil.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:7 explicitly states that the LORD forms light and creates darkness, makes peace and creates evil, showing His control over all aspects of existence.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 45 teaches that the LORD's word to the seed of Jacob is spoken in secret and darkness.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:19 clearly states that the LORD has not spoken in secret or darkness but declares righteous and right things openly to Jacob.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 45 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 45 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by God's declaration in Isaiah 45:7, where He says, "I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil"?
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence over all creation
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:7 shows God's sovereign control over all aspects of existence, including light, darkness, peace, and calamity, demonstrating His omnipotence over all creation.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 45:13, what role does God assign to Cyrus in His divine plan?
options: To build God's city and release captives without price or reward
To judge Israel for their disobedience
To conquer Israel's enemies for personal gain
questions.correctAnswer: To build God's city and release captives without price or reward
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:13 states that God raised Cyrus up in righteousness to direct his ways, build God's city, and release captives without price or reward, highlighting Cyrus' divinely appointed role.

questions.question: What theological truth about God's uniqueness is emphasized in Isaiah 45:5-6?
options: There is no God besides the LORD
God is one among many gods
God is limited by human knowledge
God is only a national deity
questions.correctAnswer: There is no God besides the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:5-6 clearly affirm the monotheistic doctrine that there is no God besides the LORD, emphasizing God's exclusive divinity and sovereignty over all.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 45:18 describe God's purpose in creating the earth, and what doctrine does this affirm?
options: The earth was created to be inhabited, affirming God as Creator with purposeful design
The earth was created by chance, affirming naturalistic origins
The earth was created for human worship alone
The earth was created as a temporary dwelling
questions.correctAnswer: The earth was created to be inhabited, affirming God as Creator with purposeful design
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:18 states that God formed the earth not in vain but to be inhabited, affirming the doctrine of purposeful creation by God as the sovereign Creator.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight is drawn from Isaiah 45:11 and Isaiah 45:12 regarding God's creative authority and providential governance?
options: God is the Holy One who commands all things and has created man and the heavens by His hands
God is distant and uninvolved in creation
God created but does not govern the universe
God depends on angels to maintain creation
questions.correctAnswer: God is the Holy One who commands all things and has created man and the heavens by His hands
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:11 and 45:12 together reveal God's sovereignty as the Holy One and Maker who commands all the heavenly hosts and created mankind, emphasizing His active providential governance.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted in Isaiah 45:15, where He is described as a God who 'hidest thyself'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's hiddenness and sovereignty
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:15 refers to God as one who hides Himself, indicating His inscrutable sovereignty and the mysteriousness of His ways beyond human understanding.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 45:22-23, what universal reality does God declare concerning all humanity?
options: Every knee shall bow and every tongue swear allegiance to the LORD
Only Israel will serve the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Every knee shall bow and every tongue swear allegiance to the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:22-23 proclaims the universal lordship of God, declaring that every knee shall bow and every tongue swear allegiance to Him, affirming His ultimate authority over all.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 45:14 illustrate God's redemptive plan in relation to Gentile nations?
options: Gentile nations will come in chains and recognize God's presence in Israel
Gentiles will remain forever in idolatry
Gentiles are excluded from God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: Gentile nations will come in chains and recognize God's presence in Israel
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:14 describes how Egypt, Ethiopia, and Sabeans will come in chains and make supplication, acknowledging that God is in Israel, showing the inclusion of Gentiles in God's redemptive plan.

questions.question: What apologetic argument does Isaiah 45:20-21 offer against idolatry and the worship of false gods?
options: Idols have no power to save, but the LORD alone is the just God and Saviour
Idols are equally powerful as the LORD
God tolerates all forms of worship
Idolatry is a valid path to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Idols have no power to save, but the LORD alone is the just God and Saviour
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:20-21 challenges idol worship by stating that idols cannot save, while the LORD is the only just God and Saviour, providing a foundation for Christian apologetics against polytheism.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching about salvation is emphasized in Isaiah 45:17 and Isaiah 45:25 when considered together?
options: Israel will receive everlasting salvation and justification in the LORD
Salvation is only for the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: Israel will receive everlasting salvation and justification in the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:17 and 45:25 together teach that Israel shall be saved with everlasting salvation and justified in the LORD, affirming God's covenantal faithfulness and grace toward His people.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 45:9 serve as a theological warning about human questioning of God’s sovereignty?
options: It warns that the creature (clay) should not dispute with the Creator (potter)
It encourages questioning God’s decisions freely
It suggests gods are subject to human will
It states that God must justify Himself to humanity
questions.correctAnswer: It warns that the creature (clay) should not dispute with the Creator (potter)
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:9 uses the analogy of clay and potter to warn against humans questioning God’s sovereign authority, emphasizing divine prerogative in creation and governance.

questions.question: What synthesis of Isaiah 45:4 and Isaiah 45:1 reveals about God's election and calling of Cyrus despite his ignorance of God?
options: God calls and names His chosen servant for His purposes even before they know Him
God only calls those who already believe
God’s election depends on human knowledge
Cyrus was unaware and therefore not chosen
questions.correctAnswer: God calls and names His chosen servant for His purposes even before they know Him
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:4 and 45:1 reveal that God elects and calls Cyrus, His anointed, before Cyrus knows Him, underscoring divine sovereignty in election and calling.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 45:19 teach about the nature of God's revelation to Israel, especially in contrast to secretive or vain searching?
options: God speaks openly and in righteousness, not in secret or vain
God's revelations are hidden and mysterious
Israel should seek God in vain
God only reveals Himself to Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: God speaks openly and in righteousness, not in secret or vain
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:19 affirms that God does not speak in secret or darkness but declares righteousness openly, assuring Israel of the validity and clarity of His revelation.

questions.question: Considering Isaiah 45:2 and 45:3 together, what theological truth is taught about God’s provision and guidance for His anointed servant?
options: God makes the way straight, breaks barriers, and provides hidden riches to His servant
God leaves His servant to struggle alone
God’s provision is limited to Israel only
God’s anointed must earn treasures through war
questions.correctAnswer: God makes the way straight, breaks barriers, and provides hidden riches to His servant
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:2-3 show God’s providential guidance and provision by straightening paths, breaking barriers, and giving hidden treasures to His anointed servant, emphasizing divine empowerment.

questions.question: From Isaiah 45:23 and 45:24, what doctrine concerning human response to God's sovereignty is taught?
options: All will ultimately bow and swear allegiance to God; those trusting in Him find righteousness and strength
Some can resist God’s will eternally
Human pride will never be humbled
Righteousness comes from human effort alone
questions.correctAnswer: All will ultimately bow and swear allegiance to God; those trusting in Him find righteousness and strength
questions.explanation: Isaiah 45:23-24 teach that every knee will bow and every tongue confess God’s lordship, and those who trust in the LORD will have righteousness and strength, highlighting human accountability and salvation.
